Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?
[2] Haley: Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.
[3] Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
[4] Max Nightriver (player): Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?
[5] Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): So who is burning the villages behind the line?
[7] Adolion Narrator: A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."
[8] Adolion Narrator: A runner in mud-splashed Crown livery is let in, whispers to Prince Forre, and is sent out again. Forre moves a black token one finger's breadth east across the map, and says nothing.
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?
[10] Forre: Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."
[11] Alexander: Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."
[12] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, what do you make of Greywater? ...Actually, never mind. Dalan, how many arrows do we have left?
[13] Dalan: Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."
[14] Max Nightriver (player): Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?
[15] Adolion Narrator: The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.
[16] Haley: Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."
[17] Max Nightriver (player): Your Majesty, who exactly would we answer to in the field, you or the Prince?
[18] Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes are hard, and he does not move from his place. "The Crown," he says, his voice low. "You answer to the Crown. In the field, that is the Prince."
He turns his gaze to Forre, and there is a flicker of something. "But the commission is mine."
A beat, and his gaze is back on the party. "And you will report to the Crown."
The King stands still, his white fur mantle catching the light, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
[19] Max Nightriver (player): Guildmaster, be straight with me. Does the Guild think this commission is worth our lives?
[20] Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Guild's thinking is this: The Crown will pay you for this job, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park." Her voice is blunt and low. "You're being sent behind their lines, and if you get caught..."
She looks at the King, her expression unreadable. "You'll be on your own."
A beat, and she looks back at the party. "The Guild thinks you can handle it. But don't mistake that for a promise you'll come back."
[21] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?
[22] Belle: Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."
[23] Max Nightriver (player): Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?
[24] Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
[25] Max Nightriver (player): Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
[26] Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."

Transcript:
[25] Max Nightriver (player): Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
[26] Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.

Transcript:
[22] Belle: Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."
[23] Max Nightriver (player): Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?
[24] Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
[25] Max Nightriver (player): Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
[26] Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.

Transcript:
[24] Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
[25] Max Nightriver (player): Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
[26] Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?
[2] Haley: Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.
[3] Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
[4] Max Nightriver (player): Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?
[5] Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): So who is burning the villages behind the line?
[7] Adolion Narrator: A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."
[8] Adolion Narrator: A runner in mud-splashed Crown livery is let in, whispers to Prince Forre, and is sent out again. Forre moves a black token one finger's breadth east across the map, and says nothing.
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?
[10] Forre: Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."
[11] Alexander: Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."
[12] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, what do you make of Greywater? ...Actually, never mind. Dalan, how many arrows do we have left?
[13] Dalan: Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."
[14] Max Nightriver (player): Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?
[15] Adolion Narrator: The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.
[16] Haley: Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."
[17] Max Nightriver (player): Your Majesty, who exactly would we answer to in the field, you or the Prince?
[18] Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes are hard, and he does not move from his place. "The Crown," he says, his voice low. "You answer to the Crown. In the field, that is the Prince."
He turns his gaze to Forre, and there is a flicker of something. "But the commission is mine."
A beat, and his gaze is back on the party. "And you will report to the Crown."
The King stands still, his white fur mantle catching the light, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
[19] Max Nightriver (player): Guildmaster, be straight with me. Does the Guild think this commission is worth our lives?
[20] Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Guild's thinking is this: The Crown will pay you for this job, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park." Her voice is blunt and low. "You're being sent behind their lines, and if you get caught..."
She looks at the King, her expression unreadable. "You'll be on your own."
A beat, and she looks back at the party. "The Guild thinks you can handle it. But don't mistake that for a promise you'll come back."
[21] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?
[22] Belle: Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."
[23] Max Nightriver (player): Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?
[24] Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
[25] Max Nightriver (player): Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
[26] Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
[32] Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.

Transcript:
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
[32] Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.
[33] Max Nightriver (player): We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.
[34] Adolion Narrator: The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

Transcript:
[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
[32] Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.
[33] Max Nightriver (player): We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.
[34] Adolion Narrator: The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

[27] Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
[29] Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
[32] Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.
[33] Max Nightriver (player): We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.
[34] Adolion Narrator: The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.

Transcript:
[30] Max Nightriver (player): Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
[31] Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
[32] Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.
[33] Max Nightriver (player): We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.
[34] Adolion Narrator: The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.
[35] Max Nightriver (player): We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.
[36] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."
[37] Adolion Narrator: The first gun speaks from across the valley just after dawn: a flat boom, a whistle, and a fountain of black earth fifty yards short of the ridge. Along the shield wall nobody flinches. They have heard it every morning for a month.

[35] Max Nightriver (player): We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.
[36] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."
[37] Adolion Narrator: The first gun speaks from across the valley just after dawn: a flat boom, a whistle, and a fountain of black earth fifty yards short of the ridge. Along the shield wall nobody flinches. They have heard it every morning for a month.
[38] Max Nightriver (player): Captain, we heard the Zegallans sent someone under a parley flag. Take us to the parley.
[39] Adolion Narrator: Captain Kaelen doesn't move at first. His gaze is hard, and his face doesn't change.
"You're under my command," he says, and his voice is low. "And I'll tell you when you're ready."
A beat, and he shifts his weight. "There is no parley."
He looks at you, and his eyes narrow. "And you're lucky I don't put you in the stocks for speaking to the Crown's army like that."
And he turns away.
The first gun speaks again: a flat boom, a whistle. And a fountain of black earth Fifty yards short of the ridge.

[40] Belle: Belle's hand goes to Cleaver's haft, and her jaw sets. "The hell he—"
She stops, and her eyes are dark. "You don't tell me when I'm ready, old man."
She looks at you, then back at the Captain. "If you're not going to take us, I'll carve my own path."

He looks at Kaelen, then at you, and he doesn't blink. "We're here to do a job. Not start another fight."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "And Captain's right. We can't just walk out."
A beat, and he looks at Max. "Not if we want to get this right."
He looks back at Kaelen, and his expression is flat. "We'll wait for the Prince."
[42] Max Nightriver (player): Then we go out under a white flag ourselves. Belle, the flag. We walk halfway down the ridge and wait for the Zegallans to send someone.
[43] Belle: "A white flag? Fuck that. I'm not some dog begging for scraps."
She looks at you. "We don't ask. We take. And if they want to talk, they'll come to us."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And if they don't, we'll give them a reason."
She turns, and her boots are heavy as she heads for the ridge.
"And as for the flag—" She stops, and looks at Dalan. "Find a white flag. We're not asking for anything."
She looks at you, and her expression is sharp. "We're just going to be there. And we'll see what they say."

[44] Kanna: Kanna drives Blood Oath into the mud, her dark red eyes narrowing. "LOUD and fuckin' plain, then. You bury yours, I bury mine. My regiment keeps Greywater. Break it and I break you. I keep my word."
The Zegallan banner flutters in the wind, and there is no mistaking the sign.
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "And you've been diggin' up our dead at Greywater, too. Some new kind of sick-fuck game?"
The black steel of her armour gleams in the dawn light. "Or maybe the Darrans finally got the balls to send in someone worth killin'."
A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"
[45] Adolion Narrator: The wind shifts, and carries the scent of iron and wet stone.
The banners of the Empire and the Crown are in sight, but there is no sound of guns, and no movement from the lines.
A beat, and the valley is quiet.
The valley is quiet.
[46] Max Nightriver (player): Blood Saint, we're not the ones digging up your dead. Why do you care where the dead go?
[47] Kanna: Kanna's eyes flicker, and a beat, her jaw sets. "Cares? I don't give a fuck about some piles of rot."
She shifts her weight, and the black steel of her armour catches the light. "What I care about is the disrespect. And the cowardice."
A beat, and her fangs show. "A soldier earns their place in the dirt. And when someone goes digging, that's an insult to every man and woman who fell."
She looks at you, her dark red eyes cold and hard. "So you Darrans can't tell me why you're diggin', and you can't tell me what you're looking for. But you're gonna tell me if you're the ones who did it."
A beat, and her hand goes to Blood Oath. "And you're gonna do it fast."

beats.title: The Ridge at Greywater
beats.objective: Hold the ridge before Greywater against the Cursefire Regiment's push, and find a way behind their lines.
beats.guidance: The Cursefire Regiment under Kanna Helfin presses the ridge with blood magic and fire. Keder Valfaust picks fighters from the Zegallan ranks and calls challenges across the gap. The party must hold long enough for Prince Forre's field army to anchor, then slip through the smoke and the dead ground to cross the Zegallan line. Vallie's warning holds: no rescue behind enemy lines. Dalan reads the forest for a path; Belle wants the ridge cleared with steel. The way behind the lines opens through the chaos of the Cursefire advance, the pits' slaving parties, or a captured Zegallan officer who knows the road to Renfath.

beats.title: Sand and Chains
beats.objective: Survive Renfath's sand and win a way out of the pits.
beats.guidance: Renfath's pits are a slaver's arena where Keder Valfaust once stood and where Shelara Kelnan of the destroyed Kelnan tribe now waits in chains. The party arrives behind the lines with no army at their back. They must fight on the sand, bargain with the pit masters, or break the pens outright. Keder keeps his word to those who earn it; the slavers do not. Shelara watches from the pens, cynical and mistrustful, a master archer who will not join anyone who leaves her people behind. The way out runs through the sand, the slave pens, or the Zegallan garrison's own corruption.

entries.text: King Alexander convened a war council where he named villages lost on the Ashen March and commissioned the party to investigate the missing dead at Greywater. Max Nightriver questioned the rumour about Queen Melisande, prompting Haley to defend her mother and the King to shut the matter down. After Vallie clarified the Guild's backing and Forre admitted the western front had slipped, the party accepted the commission and departed for Fort Vicinitas.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.
Max Nightriver: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?
Haley: Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.
Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
Max Nightriver: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?
Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."
Max Nightriver: So who is burning the villages behind the line?
Adolion Narrator: A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."
Adolion Narrator: A runner in mud-splashed Crown livery is let in, whispers to Prince Forre, and is sent out again. Forre moves a black token one finger's breadth east across the map, and says nothing.
Max Nightriver: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?
Forre: Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."
Alexander: Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."
Max Nightriver: Belle, what do you make of Greywater? ...Actually, never mind. Dalan, how many arrows do we have left?
Dalan: Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."
Max Nightriver: Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?
Adolion Narrator: The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.
Haley: Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."
Max Nightriver: Your Majesty, who exactly would we answer to in the field, you or the Prince?
Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes are hard, and he does not move from his place. "The Crown," he says, his voice low. "You answer to the Crown. In the field, that is the Prince."
He turns his gaze to Forre, and there is a flicker of something. "But the commission is mine."
A beat, and his gaze is back on the party. "And you will report to the Crown."
The King stands still, his white fur mantle catching the light, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
Max Nightriver: Guildmaster, be straight with me. Does the Guild think this commission is worth our lives?
Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Guild's thinking is this: The Crown will pay you for this job, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park." Her voice is blunt and low. "You're being sent behind their lines, and if you get caught..."
She looks at the King, her expression unreadable. "You'll be on your own."
A beat, and she looks back at the party. "The Guild thinks you can handle it. But don't mistake that for a promise you'll come back."
Max Nightriver: Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?
Belle: Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."
Max Nightriver: Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?
Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
Max Nightriver: Has anyone actually seen where the dead go after they leave their graves?
Adolion Narrator: The question hangs in the air, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room.
Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Guildmaster Vallie shifts her weight, her leather boots creaking on the stone floor.
The King stands still, his face a mask, his gaze fixed on the map table where the Zegallan banner hangs above.
A beat, and he speaks, his voice low and flat. "No one."
He looks at you, his eyes dark. "No one has seen where they go."
And the silence stretches, and the King does not look away.
Alexander: "The dead do not leave their graves," he says, and his voice is low. "The dead stay where they are placed."
He looks at you. "And we will find out where they are going."
He doesn't move, his face a mask. "And we will bring them back."
The King's voice is sharp. "And we will end this rumour."
Max Nightriver: Then we take the King's commission. Point us at the front, Your Majesty.
Alexander: Alexander's face does not soften, but there is a flicker of something in his eyes. "Very well."
He looks at Forre. "The commission is yours."
And he looks at you again. "And you will be remembered for your names."
The King turns, and his white fur mantle shifts as he walks away from the map table, his footsteps echoing in the war room.
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do not fail me."
He does not look back.
Max Nightriver: Belle, Dalan, get the horses. We ride for Fort Vicinitas tonight.
Belle: "Finally." Belle's grin is sharp, and she cracks her knuckles. "Get the horses. We'll ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn."
She glances at the map one more time, then at Forre. "We'll bring you back what you're looking for."
And she turns and leaves the war room, her boots heavy on the stone floor.
A beat, and the sound of her footsteps fades.
The room is quiet, and the smell of old banners and map parchment lingers.
Dalan: Dalan's eyes flicker to the map, then he's already moving. "The horses. Yes."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "I'll get the horses. Right away."
And he turns and leaves the war room as well, his footsteps quiet on the stone floor.
The sound of his boots fades, and the room is silent.
A beat, and Forre's emerald eyes are still on the map table, where the Zegallan token sits one finger's breadth east.
The room is quiet.

entries.text: Max Nightriver led the party west through the night, riding a cold, dark road through pine-scented hills until dawn broke over the ridge. They arrived at Fort Vicinitas, a sprawling grey stone and iron stronghold with open gates, scarred walls, and banners snapping in the wind. A sentry stood at the gate as the party approached, the scene carrying a somber, resolute tone.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We ride west through the night and reach the gates of Fort Vicinitas at dawn.
Adolion Narrator: The ride is cold, the road a dark ribbon cutting through the hills. The party's horses' hooves drum against the earth, and the scent of pine and wet grass follows them.
The first light of dawn breaks over the ridge, painting the sky in shades of grey and pale blue.
And there, at the edge of the ridge, sits Fort Vicinitas—a sprawl of grey stone and iron, its banners snapping in the wind, and its gates open wide.
The stone walls rise high, their faces scored with the scars of old wars, and the air is thick with the smell of horse sweat and woodsmoke.
A sentry stands at the gate, his spear-tip catching the first light.

entries.text: Max Nightriver and the party entered Fort Vicinitas and were confronted by Captain Kaelen, who declared they were under his command until the Prince arrived at noon. When Max demanded to be taken to a Zegallan parley, Kaelen coldly denied any parley existed and threatened him with the stocks.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We ride through the gate and report to whoever commands Fort Vicinitas.
Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves clatter on the stone as the party passes through the gate. The sentry steps aside, his spear-tip lowered.
The courtyard is empty, save for a few soldiers who are just stirring.
A man in plate armour stands at the far end of the courtyard, his face grim and his eyes hard. He is watching the party approach.
His armour is scarred and dented, and a longsword hangs at his hip.
He does not move as the party approaches, but his gaze is fixed on them.
And his voice is low and flat.
"You're the Crown's free company."
He doesn't wait for an answer.
"I am Captain Kaelen. I command this fort."
He looks at the party, his gaze lingering on Belle and Dalan.
"The Prince will be here by noon. Until then, you are under my command."
He looks at you.
"And we have much to discuss."
Adolion Narrator: The first gun speaks from across the valley just after dawn: a flat boom, a whistle, and a fountain of black earth fifty yards short of the ridge. Along the shield wall nobody flinches. They have heard it every morning for a month.
Max Nightriver: Captain, we heard the Zegallans sent someone under a parley flag. Take us to the parley.
Adolion Narrator: Captain Kaelen doesn't move at first. His gaze is hard, and his face doesn't change.
"You're under my command," he says, and his voice is low. "And I'll tell you when you're ready."
A beat, and he shifts his weight. "There is no parley."
He looks at you, and his eyes narrow. "And you're lucky I don't put you in the stocks for speaking to the Crown's army like that."
And he turns away.
The first gun speaks again: a flat boom, a whistle. And a fountain of black earth Fifty yards short of the ridge.

entries.text: Max Nightriver proposed going out under a white flag to meet the Zegallans, but Belle rejected asking for anything and headed for the ridge, telling Dalan to find a white flag so they would simply be there. Dalan urged Belle to wait, insisting they were there to do a job and that they should wait for the Prince as Kaelen had said. At the ridge, Kanna drove Blood Oath into the mud and declared that each side buries its own dead, that her regiment keeps Greywater, and that she would break anyone who broke that, then accused the Darrans of digging up Zegallan dead at Greywater. Max denied it and asked why she cared where the dead go, and Kanna answered that she cared about the disrespect and cowardice of digging up soldiers who had earned their place in the dirt, demanding to know if the Darrans were responsible. Belle told Kanna it was not them, that they were on a Crown job looking for the missing dead, and suggested both sides might share the same problem. Max asked Kanna to swear on Blood Oath that her regiment had not taken the dead, and Kanna swore the Cursefire Regiment had not, then demanded Max swear on Cleaver, threatening to take his head if he lied and offering his own if she lied.
entries.evidence:
Belle: Belle's hand goes to Cleaver's haft, and her jaw sets. "The hell he—"
She stops, and her eyes are dark. "You don't tell me when I'm ready, old man."
She looks at you, then back at the Captain. "If you're not going to take us, I'll carve my own path."
And she doesn't wait. She turns on her heel, and her boots are heavy on the stone floor as she heads for the gate.
Dalan: Dalan is already looking toward the gate, and his gaze is sharp.
"Belle." He says it quiet, but there is an edge. "Wait."
He looks at Kaelen, then at you, and he doesn't blink. "We're here to do a job. Not start another fight."
He shifts his weight, and his cheeks go pink. "And Captain's right. We can't just walk out."
A beat, and he looks at Max. "Not if we want to get this right."
He looks back at Kaelen, and his expression is flat. "We'll wait for the Prince."
Max Nightriver: Then we go out under a white flag ourselves. Belle, the flag. We walk halfway down the ridge and wait for the Zegallans to send someone.
Belle: "A white flag? Fuck that. I'm not some dog begging for scraps."
She looks at you. "We don't ask. We take. And if they want to talk, they'll come to us."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And if they don't, we'll give them a reason."
She turns, and her boots are heavy as she heads for the ridge.
"And as for the flag—" She stops, and looks at Dalan. "Find a white flag. We're not asking for anything."
She looks at you, and her expression is sharp. "We're just going to be there. And we'll see what they say."
Kanna: Kanna drives Blood Oath into the mud, her dark red eyes narrowing. "LOUD and fuckin' plain, then. You bury yours, I bury mine. My regiment keeps Greywater. Break it and I break you. I keep my word."
The Zegallan banner flutters in the wind, and there is no mistaking the sign.
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "And you've been diggin' up our dead at Greywater, too. Some new kind of sick-fuck game?"
The black steel of her armour gleams in the dawn light. "Or maybe the Darrans finally got the balls to send in someone worth killin'."
A beat, and her voice drops. "Which one is it?"
Adolion Narrator: The wind shifts, and carries the scent of iron and wet stone.
The banners of the Empire and the Crown are in sight, but there is no sound of guns, and no movement from the lines.

Kanna: Kanna's eyes flicker, and a beat, her jaw sets. "Cares? I don't give a fuck about some piles of rot."
She shifts her weight, and the black steel of her armour catches the light. "What I care about is the disrespect. And the cowardice."
A beat, and her fangs show. "A soldier earns their place in the dirt. And when someone goes digging, that's an insult to every man and woman who fell."

arcs.text: The party must answer the King's commission and decide whether to take the Crown's offer of a free company.
Villages on the Ashen March have been lost, and the war against Zegalla presses on the Darran Kingdom.
The party must answer the King's demand for acceptance or refusal of the commission, to his face.
arcs.summary: King Alexander demanded the party answer his commission to their faces, offering a Crown contract as a free company under the Guild's charter to travel to Greywater and the Ashen March and investigate the missing dead. Prince Forre had marked a road to Fort Vicinitas on the map table, but when he openly told the King that the Darran Kingdom was losing the war, Alexander rebuked him and denied the western front had slipped a mile and a half, insisting the line would hold at Fort Vicinitas. The King ordered the party to go to Greywater to find the missing dead and end the rumour of the winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr, who was burning villages behind the Darran line as an Imperial weapon the Empire could not control. Vallie Goredust described the commission as sending the party behind enemy lines as a scalpel force, with the Guild backing them but no rescue if they were caught, and the party accepted the King's demand for an answer.

The party must now march to the front under Prince Forre's command as a Crown free company and find where the missing dead go.
The King has charged the party not to fail him, and the true state of the line at Fort Vicinitas remains contested.
Prince Forre openly admits he keeps the Queen's rumour burning for his own advantage, deepening the rift with the King and Princess.

Kanna accuses the Darrans of digging up Zegallan dead at Greywater, and demands the party answer for it before the parley can continue.
The mystery of who is digging up the dead now cuts both ways — the Zegallans are also missing bodies, and Kanna wants answers.
Kanna's Blood Oath and her demand that Max swear on Cleaver leave the parley balanced on a knife's edge — one lie and blood is owed.
Both sides are missing their dead, and neither yet knows who is taking them.
The truce over Greywater's graves is sworn but unproven — both sides still hunt whoever is digging up the dead, and either could blame the other.

canon.text:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
King Alexander summoned the party before his war council and demanded they answer his commission to their faces. He offered them a Crown contract as a free company under the Guild's charter, ordering them to travel to Greywater and the Ashen March to investigate the missing dead and to end the rumour of the winged herald, a self-styled servant of Prodyr who was burning villages behind the Darran line as an Imperial weapon the Empire could not control. Prince Forre marked a road to Fort Vicinitas on the map table and openly told the King that the Darran Kingdom was losing the war, but Alexander rebuked him, denied the western front had slipped a mile and a half and cost ten villages, and insisted the line would hold at Fort Vicinitas. Vallie Goredust explained that the commission was for a scalpel force to slip behind Zegallan lines where Prince Forre's army could not go, with the Crown paying and the Guild backing them but no rescue if they were caught. Queen Melisande's seat at the war council sat empty, a raw subject for the royal family; Princess Haley denied the rumours about her mother and insisted she was not a necromancer, while Prince Forre refused to suppress the rumour, saying he would not extinguish fires that warm his house. The party resolved to accept the commission.

CURRENT STATE:
The party has accepted the King's commission and will ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn. The commission remains active and unresolved in its execution: they are to go to Greywater and the Ashen March to find the missing dead and end the rumour of the winged herald. The western front remains contested, with Alexander insisting the line will hold at Fort Vicinitas even as Forre maintains the kingdom is losing the war. The winged herald, a servant of Prodyr whom the Empire cannot control, continues to burn villages behind the Darran line. No one has seen where the missing dead go after they leave their graves. The rumour about Queen Melisande remains alive, deliberately kept so by Prince Forre for his own purposes, and Princess Haley continues to deny it. Dalan has counted the party's arrows at forty-eight, thirty-six standard and twelve for piercing, judging it enough to hunt one or two monsters but not to fight out of an army. Belle has vowed to put her axe in the winged herald's skull if he shows himself.

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
King Alexander rules the Darran Kingdom and refuses to admit the western front has slipped, insisting the line will hold at Fort Vicinitas. Prince Forre is his son, assigned the commission, and openly holds that the kingdom is losing the war; he deliberately keeps the rumour about Queen Melisande alive, calling it a fire that warms his house. Queen Melisande's seat at the war council sits empty, a raw subject for the royal family. Princess Haley denies the rumours about her mother and insists she is not a necromancer, and forbids speaking of her that way. Vallie Goredust is the Guildmaster who framed the commission: the Crown wants a scalpel, adventurers to go behind enemy lines where the army cannot, unsupported if caught, with the Crown paying and the Guild backing them but no rescue behind enemy lines. The winged herald calls himself a servant of Prodyr, burns villages behind the Darran line, and is an Imperial weapon the Empire cannot control. The western front has slipped a mile and a half, costing ten villages. The party possesses forty-eight arrows, thirty-six standard and twelve for piercing. The party will ride for Fort Vicinitas before dawn.

removed.text: King Alexander named the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marked a road to Fort Vicinitas, and Vallie presented the Guild charter for a free company. Max Nightriver asked Princess Haley about a rumour concerning her mother, and Haley called it childish and base before falling silent. Alexander declared the matter a war council, not a gossip's den, and asked the party to accept a commission involving Greywater, the Ashen March, and the missing dead. Vallie explained the Crown wanted a scalpel to send behind enemy lines, and Alexander identified a winged herald claiming to serve Prodyr as the Empire's weapon burning villages. After a runner whispered to Forre, Forre said the western front had moved a mile and a half and told the King they were losing the war, but Alexander insisted the line would hold at Fort Vicinitas and told the party to go to Greywater to find the missing dead and end the rumour.
removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.
Max Nightriver: Princess Haley, do you believe the rumour about your mother?
Haley: Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.
Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
Max Nightriver: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?
Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."
Max Nightriver: So who is burning the villages behind the line?
Adolion Narrator: A murmur passes through the councillors. Haley's hand tightens on her fan, and Forre's green eyes flicker to the King.
"A winged herald calling himself a servant of Prodyr," Alexander says, his voice cold. "He claims to be a divine messenger. The villages he burns are—" He doesn't finish. "He is the Empire's weapon."
Vallie's eye narrows. "One he can't control." She glances at the party. "And that's why they want you. Soldiers fight armies. You hunt monsters."
Adolion Narrator: A runner in mud-splashed Crown livery is let in, whispers to Prince Forre, and is sent out again. Forre moves a black token one finger's breadth east across the map, and says nothing.
Max Nightriver: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?
Forre: Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."
Alexander: Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."

removed.evidence:
Max Nightriver: Belle, what do you make of Greywater? ...Actually, never mind. Dalan, how many arrows do we have left?
Dalan: Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."
Max Nightriver: Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?
Adolion Narrator: The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.
Haley: Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."
Max Nightriver: Your Majesty, who exactly would we answer to in the field, you or the Prince?
Alexander: Alexander's dark eyes are hard, and he does not move from his place. "The Crown," he says, his voice low. "You answer to the Crown. In the field, that is the Prince."
He turns his gaze to Forre, and there is a flicker of something. "But the commission is mine."
A beat, and his gaze is back on the party. "And you will report to the Crown."
The King stands still, his white fur mantle catching the light, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"
Max Nightriver: Guildmaster, be straight with me. Does the Guild think this commission is worth our lives?
Vallie: Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Guild's thinking is this: The Crown will pay you for this job, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park." Her voice is blunt and low. "You're being sent behind their lines, and if you get caught..."
She looks at the King, her expression unreadable. "You'll be on your own."
A beat, and she looks back at the party. "The Guild thinks you can handle it. But don't mistake that for a promise you'll come back."
Max Nightriver: Belle, you've been quiet. What do you think of this King and his war?
Belle: Belle's jaw sets, and she shifts her weight. "The King's right to call us a scalpel," she says, her voice flat. "Forre's hammer will smash everything, but it won't find what we're looking for."
She looks at Max, then at the map. "We'll go behind the lines, find what's missing, and bring it back."
A beat, and her grin is all teeth. "And I'll have my axe in the skulls of that winged herald if he shows his face."
Max Nightriver: Prince Forre, you let that rumour about the Queen run through camp. Why haven't you put it down?
Forre: Forre's green eyes flicker up from the map, and he doesn't smile. "A rumour is a fire. You don't put it out by pouring water on it. You starve it of oxygen."
He looks back at the map, his finger tracing the line of the token. "And I am not in the business of extinguishing fires that warm my house."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The court speaks. The court whispers. The court lies."
He doesn't say anything else.
